facts.text: Mucha's posters carry his signature printed in the lithographic stone, often with the printer's name elsewhere on the sheet; Princeton's Job poster of 1897 is 'Signed in stone, lower right: Mucha' with F. Champenois, Paris, at lower left.
On the National Gallery of Art's Biscuits Lefèvre-Utile poster (1896) 'Mucha' is printed on the stone at lower left, with 'F. Champenois. Paris.' at bottom centre.
After the success of his Gismonda poster for Sarah Bernhardt, Mucha signed an exclusive contract with the printer Champenois for commercial and decorative posters.

items.medium: colour lithograph on paper laid down on linen
items.note: Printer's line 'F. Champenois. Paris.' is at bottom centre.
Reduced reprint published in Les Maîtres de l'Affiche (plate 114); the poster text is dated MDCCCXCVI.
